The most seismic activity happens during high tides (of the oceans) and low tides. Yesterday was an extremely low tide period. Why is this? Because the moon has a slight gravitational pull on the surface of the earth, so when it is closest to the earth (about once a month at a full moon), it will pull on the surface of the earth. The water in the ocean demonstrates this gravitational pull, with monthly high tides and low tides. The land is also subject to this gravitational pull, so if seismic pressure has built up on any fault line this additional gravitational pull can be just enough to trigger a quake, either lots of small ones, or one big one, if the area has been "locked" for awhile (no small quakes at all).

That's about all you need to know, except before a sizable quake happens, some animals will be disturbed, like run under the bed before a quake and won't come out. It is picking up on high pitched sounds or something we humans do not pick up. Birds will cling to the side of a bird cage right before a quake happens. In China it was noted that snakes were very active (getting out of the area) before a large quake hit. In Japan they have noticed that a super deep water ocean fish, the oar fish, will surface and beach itself. (Japan is surrounded by water.) So the sighting of these oar fish on the beach or on the surface of the water, is an omen that a quake might be coming.

The best thing to do, is get prepared. Go outside where you live, and examine the possible hazards of any falling debris that might fall on you if a quake gets big enough, you decide to make a run for it outside. Will you be hit by broken glass from above (in a high rise building)? Will you be hit by falling power lines? Don't take an elevator down. Its best to take the stairs.
